title: Signal Drift

selected_categories.reasoning: The game is an endless score-attack run with continuously spawning threats, implied forward motion, escalating pace, and immediate restart loops.
The player only steers horizontally while objects approach from above, and the visuals even suggest lane divisions, though movement is smooth rather than strictly lane-snapped.
The main objective is survival under increasing pressure, with one-hit failure and run longevity directly tied to player performance.
The presentation features glowing futuristic UI, bright signal pickups, and a stylized sci-fi arcade aesthetic that partially aligns with neon-runner conventions.
The game takes place in an abstract dark space-like field with minimal environmental grounding, making a void-runner framing plausible.

uncertainty_notes: No category perfectly matches a one-axis collect-and-dodge arcade survival game, so the best-fit ranking leans on runner and survival analogies.
It is not a strict lane-switcher because the player follows continuous pointer movement.
The game does not emphasize jumping, terrain traversal, or stage completion, so runner labels are thematic/mechanical approximations rather than exact genre matches.
